'''Devarajan (Dave) Thirumalai''', an Indian-born American physicist, is the Collie-Welch Reagents Professor in Chemistry at the [[University of Texas at Austin]]. His research spans equilibrium and non-equilibrium statistical mechanics, such as the transition from liquid to
amorphous state, polymer-colloid interactions, and protein and RNA folding. He is known for his contributions to the theories of protein/RNA folding,<ref name=ThirumalaiScience95/><ref name=ThirumalaiBiochemistry05/> protein aggregation,<ref name=Thirumalaicurrent03/> glasses (the Random First Order Transition – RFOT theory),<ref name = ThirumalaiPhysical89/><ref name=RFOT/> and biological machines.<ref name=Thirumalaireview20/> He also does research in intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs),<ref name=Thirumalaijpcb19/> organization and dynamics of chromosome,<ref name=Thirumalainat18/> cell biophysics<ref name=Thirumalaiprx18/> and developmental biology,<ref name = Thirumalainat25/><ref name=ThirumalaieLife24/>,.<ref name=ThirumalaieLife21/> Prior to moving to the [[University of Texas at Austin]], he was a distinguished university professor in the [[University of Maryland]] from 2010 to 2015.

==Educational Background==
Dave Thirumalai studied at the [[Indian Institute of Technology, Kanpur]] where he earned a [[Master of Science|MSc]] degree (1977).  He earned his doctorate degree in 1982 from the [[University of Minnesota]] under [[Donald G. Truhlar]].

==Academic career==
After postdoctoral studies at the [[Columbia University]] in [[New York City]], he joined University of Maryland as an assistant professor of physics in 1985. He is the founding director of the biophysics program in the [[University of Maryland]]. In 2016, he joined the [[University of Texas at Austin]] as the Collie-Welch Reagents Chair.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cm.utexas.edu/news/entry/dave-thirumalai-to-chair-department-of-chemistry| title=Dave Thirumalai to Chair Department of Chemistry}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
*1986–1988 Alfred P. Sloan Fellowship.
*1987–1992 Presidential Young Investigator Award.
*2009 Humboldt Research Award for Senior U.S. Scientists.
*2009 Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry.
*2011 Honorary Senior Hans-Fisher Fellow.
*2014 Fellow of the Biophysical Society.
*2015 Fellow of the American Physical Society.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=2015&unit_id=DBIO&institution=| title=2015 APS Fellow Archive}}</ref>
*2016 Chemical Research Society of India (CRSI) Medal.
*2016 ACS Theoretical Chemistry Award.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://phys-acs.org/awards/2016.html| title=2016 Physical Chemistry Division Awards}}</ref>
*2018 Oesper Award, Chemistry, University of Cincinnati.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cm.utexas.edu/news/entry/thirumalai-receives| title=Dave Thirumalai Receives 2018 Oesper Award}}</ref>
*2019 APS Award, Irving Langmuir Prize.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cns.utexas.edu/news/accolades/dave-thirumalai-awarded-langmuir-prize-chemical-physics|title=Dave Thirumalai Awarded Langmuir Prize in Chemical Physics}}</ref>
*2019 Hans Neurath Award, Protein Society.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cm.utexas.edu/news/entry/thirumalai-receives-1|title=Dave Thirumalai Receives the Hans Neurath Award}}</ref>
*2025 Founders Award, Biophysical Society.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.biophysics.org/news-room/devarajan-thirumalai-to-receive-biophysical-societys-2025-founders-award|title=Devarajan Thirumalai to Receive Biophysical Society's 2025 Founders Award}}</ref>
*2025 Max Delbrück Prize,  American Physical Society.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://chemistry.utexas.edu/news/accolades/devarajan-thirumalai-receives-max-delbruck-prize-biological-physics|title=Devarajan Thirumalai Receives Max Delbrück Prize in Biological Physics}}</ref>
